questions.knowledgeNote: Ordered pairs are equal iff first components match AND second components match — order matters, unlike sets.
questions.question: Q1(a). Identify whether (1,3) and (3,1) are equal.
questions.solution: First components: 1 ≠ 3, so the pairs differ already. ✅ NOT equal. (Never swap-check sets here — (1,3) ≠ (3,1) is the canonical example.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics XI, Ch.2 Book Ex 2.1 Q1(a)

questions.knowledgeNote: Identical pairs are trivially equal — the reflexive case examiners include to test the definition.
questions.question: Q1(b). Identify whether (a,b) and (a,b) are equal.
questions.solution: First: a = a; second: b = b. ✅ Equal.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics XI, Ch.2 Book Ex 2.1 Q1(b)

questions.knowledgeNote: Distinct symbols denote distinct entries unless an equation says otherwise: a ≠ x as printed.
questions.question: Q1(c). Identify whether (1,a) and (1,x) are equal.
questions.solution: First components match (1 = 1) but second components a, x are distinct symbols with no relation given. ✅ NOT equal.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics XI, Ch.2 Book Ex 2.1 Q1(c)

questions.knowledgeNote: (x,x) = (y,y) would force x = y by both components — with x, y unrelated, they differ.
questions.question: Q1(d). Identify whether (x,x) and (y,y) are equal.
questions.solution: Equality would require x = y (first components) and x = y (second) — not given. ✅ NOT equal.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics XI, Ch.2 Book Ex 2.1 Q1(d)

questions.knowledgeNote: Equate components to get a 2×2 linear system; add the equations to kill y.
questions.question: Q2(a). Find x and y if (x+y, 3) = (1, x−y).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics XI, Ch.2 Book Ex 2.1 Q2(a)

questions.knowledgeNote: Same method with messier coefficients — substitute y from the simpler equation.
questions.question: Q2(b). Find x and y if (x+2y, 3) = (−1, 2x−y).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics XI, Ch.2 Book Ex 2.1 Q2(b)

questions.knowledgeNote: Decoupled equations — read each variable straight off.
questions.question: Q2(c). Find x and y if (x−2, y+1) = (1, 0).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics XI, Ch.2 Book Ex 2.1 Q2(c)

questions.knowledgeNote: Watch the sign: −3 = y+3 gives y = −6, not +6.
questions.question: Q2(d). Find x and y if (2x−1, −3) = (1, y+3).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics XI, Ch.2 Book Ex 2.1 Q2(d)

questions.knowledgeNote: A×A lists every first-set element against every first-set element: n(A)² pairs.
questions.question: Q3(a). If A = {1,2,3} and B = {a,b}, find A × A.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics XI, Ch.2 Book Ex 2.1 Q3(a)

questions.knowledgeNote: Same construction on the 2-element set: 2² = 4 pairs.
questions.question: Q3(b). With A, B as above, find B × B.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics XI, Ch.2 Book Ex 2.1 Q3(b)

questions.knowledgeNote: Order matters: B×A ≠ A×B. The web index quotes 'B × A' but solves A × B — both products are given so the printed answer is covered either way.
questions.question: Q3(c). With A, B as above, find B × A (web index prints 'B × A'; its worked solution shows A × B — both given).
questions.solution: B × A (first from B, second from A) = {(a,1),(a,2),(a,3),(b,1),(b,2),(b,3)} — 6 pairs. For reference, A × B = {(1,a),(1,b),(2,a),(2,b),(3,a),(3,b)}. ✅ (Flag: confirm which product the printed book asks — the two differ by order throughout.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics XI, Ch.2 Book Ex 2.1 Q3(c); order ambiguity flagged vs the web index

questions.knowledgeNote: Union first, then cross: B∪C = {b,c,d}, and A supplies the first components.
questions.question: Q4(a). Let A = {a,b}, B = {b,c}, C = {c,d}. Find A × (B ∪ C).
questions.solution: B∪C = {b,c,d}. A×(B∪C) = {(a,b),(a,c),(a,d),(b,b),(b,c),(b,d)} — 6 pairs. ✅ (Web-index typo fixed: it prints (b,a), but a ∉ B∪C, so (b,a) is impossible; the correct pair is (b,b).)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics XI, Ch.2 Book Ex 2.1 Q4(a)

questions.knowledgeNote: Intersection first: only c survives B∩C, so just 2 pairs.
questions.question: Q4(b). With A, B, C as above, find A × (B ∩ C).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics XI, Ch.2 Book Ex 2.1 Q4(b)

questions.knowledgeNote: Distributive law preview: this union must equal Q4(a) — use it as a cross-check.
questions.question: Q4(c). With A, B, C as above, find (A × B) ∪ (A × C).
questions.solution: A×B = {(a,b),(a,c),(b,b),(b,c)}; A×C = {(a,c),(a,d),(b,c),(b,d)}. Union = {(a,b),(a,c),(a,d),(b,b),(b,c),(b,d)} — identical to Q4(a), as A×(B∪C) = (A×B)∪(A×C) demands. ✅
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics XI, Ch.2 Book Ex 2.1 Q4(c)

questions.knowledgeNote: Only pairs present in BOTH products survive: the ones whose second component is c.
questions.question: Q4(d). With A, B, C as above, find (A × B) ∩ (A × C).
questions.solution: Common to {(a,b),(a,c),(b,b),(b,c)} and {(a,c),(a,d),(b,c),(b,d)}: (a,c) and (b,c). ✅ {(a,c),(b,c)}. (Web index omits the comma — restored.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics XI, Ch.2 Book Ex 2.1 Q4(d)

questions.knowledgeNote: LHS–RHS verification: compute both sides fully, then compare as sets.
questions.question: Q5(a). Let A = {a,b}, B = {c,d}, C = {d,e}. Verify A × (B ∪ C) = (A × B) ∪ (A × C).
questions.solution: LHS: B∪C = {c,d,e}; A×that = {(a,c),(a,d),(a,e),(b,c),(b,d),(b,e)}. RHS: (A×B)∪(A×C) = {(a,c),(a,d),(b,c),(b,d)} ∪ {(a,d),(a,e),(b,d),(b,e)} = {(a,c),(a,d),(a,e),(b,c),(b,d),(b,e)}. LHS = RHS. ✅ Verified.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics XI, Ch.2 Book Ex 2.1 Q5(a)

questions.knowledgeNote: Same drill for ∩: B∩C = {d} collapses the LHS to 2 pairs.
questions.question: Q5(b). With A, B, C as above, verify A × (B ∩ C) = (A × B) ∩ (A × C).
questions.solution: LHS: B∩C = {d}; A×{d} = {(a,d),(b,d)}. RHS: {(a,c),(a,d),(b,c),(b,d)} ∩ {(a,d),(a,e),(b,d),(b,e)} = {(a,d),(b,d)}. LHS = RHS. ✅ Verified.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics XI, Ch.2 Book Ex 2.1 Q5(b)

questions.knowledgeNote: Build B by evaluating the rule at each x in A — B's order follows x = 1, 2, 3.
questions.question: Q6(a). Find the Cartesian product A × B where A = {x : x = 1,2,3} and B = {y : y = 3−x}.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics XI, Ch.2 Book Ex 2.1 Q6(a)

questions.knowledgeNote: Squares grow fast: x = 2 gives y = 4, so B is not {0,1,2}.
questions.question: Q6(b). Find A × B where A = {x : x = 0,1,2} and B = {y : y = x²}.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics XI, Ch.2 Book Ex 2.1 Q6(b)
